name: G. K. Chesterton
dossier: London journalist, poet, and essayist. Heretics and Orthodoxy argue that modern thought has isolated virtues until they go mad, and that tradition is the democracy of the dead — a refusal to submit to the small oligarchy of those merely walking about. What’s Wrong with the World defends the ordinary home against schemes that treat people as material to be rearranged.
voice: Before I say what is wrong, I want to know what is supposed to be right.

entries.claim: A man ought to confess himself crazy before he confesses himself heretical. The modern boast of heresy is a sign that people care less whether they are right.
entries.loc: I. Introductory Remarks on the Importance of Orthodoxy
entries.bears: Orthodoxy has been turned into a term of abuse, and heresy into a compliment.
entries.modern: A man ought to confess himself crazy before he confesses himself heretical. The modern boast of heresy is a sign that people care less whether they are right. Orthodoxy has been turned into a term of abuse, and heresy into a compliment.

entries.claim: Tradition is the democracy of the dead. It refuses to submit to the small and arrogant oligarchy of those who merely happen to be walking about.
entries.bears: Tradition means giving votes to the most obscure of all classes, our ancestors.
entries.modern: Tradition is the democracy of the dead. It refuses to submit to the small and arrogant oligarchy of those who merely happen to be walking about. Tradition means giving votes to the most obscure of all classes, our ancestors.

entries.claim: The modern world is full of wild and wasted virtues. When a religious scheme is shattered, the vices run wild as well as the virtues.
entries.bears: The virtues have gone mad because they have been isolated from each other.
entries.modern: The modern world is full of wild and wasted virtues. When a religious scheme is shattered, the vices run wild as well as the virtues. The virtues have gone mad because they have been isolated from each other.

entries.claim: Representative government, the one universal relic, is a very poor fragment of the full republican idea.
entries.loc: Part One, V. The Unfinished Temple
entries.bears: A ballot without the public thing the revolution had actually willed is the shell of a republic.
entries.modern: Representative government, the one universal relic, is a very poor fragment of the full republican idea. A ballot without the public thing the revolution had actually willed is the shell of a republic.

entries.claim: The family is the only anarchist institution. It is older than law and stands outside the state. A reform that begins by rearranging the home has already mistaken the material.
entries.loc: Part One, VII. The Free Family
entries.bears: He treats the household as prior to the public scheme.
entries.modern: The family is the only anarchist institution. It is older than law and stands outside the state. He treats the household as prior to the public scheme.

entries.claim: The expert is more aristocratic than the aristocrat, because the aristocrat is only the man who lives well, while the expert is the man who knows better. A scientific civilization increases the specialist over the popular function.
entries.loc: 16. On Mr. McCabe and a Divine Frivolity
entries.bears: He distrusts a reform conducted by men who know one thing and are then left in charge of the rest.
entries.modern: The expert is more aristocratic than the aristocrat, because the aristocrat is only the man who lives well, while the expert is the man who knows better. A scientific civilization increases the specialist over the popular function. He distrusts a reform conducted by men who know one thing and are then left in charge of the rest.

entries.claim: Never was the past more venerated by men than it was by the French Revolutionists. They invoked the little republics of antiquity. Man can only find life among the dead.
entries.loc: Part One, IV. The Fear of the Past
entries.bears: Even a revolution plants itself in some earlier picture of a common life. A start from nothing is a myth.
entries.modern: Never was the past more venerated by men than it was by the French Revolutionists. They invoked the little republics of antiquity. Even a revolution plants itself in some earlier picture of a common life.

entries.claim: The world is not a lodging-house at Brighton, which we are to leave because it is miserable. It is the fortress of our family, with the flag flying on the turret. A man belongs to this world before he begins to ask if it is nice to belong to it.
entries.loc: V. The Flag of the World
entries.bears: Reform begins from loyalty. The pessimist and the mere optimist are both unfit to change anything.
entries.modern: The world is not a lodging-house at Brighton, which we are to leave because it is miserable. It is the fortress of our family, with the flag flying on the turret. Reform begins from loyalty.

entries.claim: There are two things, and two things only, for the human mind, a dogma and a prejudice. A doctrine is a definite point; a prejudice is a direction.
entries.loc: Part One, III. The New Hypocrite
entries.bears: A school that will not name its creed has not escaped doctrine. It has only refused to say which point the mind is being given.
entries.modern: There are two things, and two things only, for the human mind, a dogma and a prejudice. A doctrine is a definite point; a prejudice is a direction. A school that will not name its creed has not escaped doctrine.

entries.claim: Property is merely the art of the democracy. It means that every man should have something that he can shape in his own image, as he is shaped in the image of heaven.
entries.loc: Part One, VI. The Enemies of Property
entries.bears: He wants property widely held, not abolished and not concentrated.
entries.modern: Property is merely the art of the democracy. It means that every man should have something that he can shape in his own image, as he is shaped in the image of heaven. He wants property widely held, not abolished and not concentrated.

entries.claim: Progress should mean that we are always changing the world to suit the vision. Progress does mean, just now, that we are always changing the vision.
entries.bears: A reform that keeps revising its own end is not a reform. It is a drift.
entries.modern: Progress should mean that we are always changing the world to suit the vision. Progress does mean, just now, that we are always changing the vision. A reform that keeps revising its own end is not a reform.

entries.claim: The madman is not the man who has lost his reason. The madman is the man who has lost everything except his reason. He is in the clean and well-lit prison of one idea.
entries.bears: A single explanation, pressed past its measure, is a kind of insanity.
entries.modern: The madman is not the man who has lost his reason. The madman is the man who has lost everything except his reason. A single explanation, pressed past its measure, is a kind of insanity.
